title: Head-centred payload update
statement: Let $c$ be a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes on a binary input $x$, let $a$ be a one-step action, let $z\in\mathbb{Z}$, and let $i$ be one of the $k+1$ virtual tape coordinates. The payload at offset $z$ and coordinate $i$ in the configuration after applying $a$ equals the payload obtained from the original configuration after first accounting for the write prescribed by $a$ and then shifting by the direction assigned to coordinate $i$ by that action, with the input-coordinate shift clipped at the input boundaries.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes on binary input $x$
$a$ is a one-step action for that machine
$i$ is an index in the $k+1$ virtual tape coordinates
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a binary machine with $k$ work tapes, let $\alpha$ be an
action, let $z$ be an integer offset, and let $i$ be one of the $k+1$ virtual tape
coordinates.  Then the head-centered payload of the configuration obtained by applying
$\alpha$ to $c$, at offset $z$ and coordinate $i$, equals the written payload of $c$
and $\alpha$ at offset $z$ plus the shift direction of coordinate $i$: writing at the
old origin and then shifting each virtual tape by its displacement produces exactly
the payloads of the successor configuration, including stationary moves, boundary
attempts, and blank writes.
